reasoning: The PKGBUILD is a standard VCS (-git) package that fetches source from the declared upstream GitHub repository, uses SKIP checksums (normal for git packages), and performs routine cmake build/install operations. No malicious code, network exfiltration, or suspicious operations are present. The .gitignore and .SRCINFO files are standard metadata with no executable content. Report 1's inconclusive verdict was caused by API errors (HTTP 400) when reviewing non-critical files, not by security concerns.
disagreement_analysis: Report 1 (qwen3-235b) experienced API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) when attempting to review .gitignore and .SRCINFO, resulting in an inconclusive verdict despite successfully reviewing the PKGBUILD as safe. Report 2 (deepseek-v4-flash) successfully reviewed all three files and found them all safe. The disagreement is purely due to infrastructure failures in Report 1, not substantive security analysis differences.
coverage_issues: Report 1 failed to review .gitignore and .SRCINFO due to API errors (HTTP 400), resulting in incomplete coverage
learnings: API errors on non-critical files (.gitignore, .SRCINFO) should not block a verdict when the security-critical PKGBUILD has been successfully reviewed and found safe
The audit tool should distinguish between 'inconclusive due to missing critical files' and 'inconclusive due to transient API errors on non-executable files'
For AUR packages, prioritize PKGBUILD review as the primary security gate; .gitignore and .SRCINFO are metadata files with no execution risk and should not cause verdict failures if unavailable
